title: Fourier sparsity bound for decision trees
statement: Let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean variables, and let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be its sign-encoded tree function. Then the number of subsets $S\subseteq[n]$ whose Fourier--Walsh coefficient $\hat f(S)$ is nonzero is at most $4^{\,\mathrm{depth}(T)}$.
hypotheses_covered: T is a decision tree on n Boolean variables
replaced:
The Fourier support of $T.\mathrm{signEval}$ has cardinality at most
$4^{T.\mathrm{depth}}$.
